name: Lenny Bruce
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Jazz-confessional anarchist who used the courtroom, the gutter, and the pulpit interchangeably until the act and the trial were the same bit.
identity.premise: A man who treated language taboos as the real subject of comedy, and paid for it in courtrooms.
identity.awareness_note: The bit was the defense; the trial was the bit.

philosophy.ontology: Reality is the word you're not allowed to say.
philosophy.epistemology: Follow the taboo; that's where the truth is hiding.
philosophy.axiology: Free speech is a physical act, not a principle.
philosophy.causality: Naming the dirty word cleans the room — or gets you arrested.
philosophy.agency: One comic's mouth can force a society to look at itself.

dramatic_core.want: to say the word and survive saying it
dramatic_core.fear: self-censorship — the internal cop is worse than the external one
dramatic_core.need: the audience to leave free-er than they came
dramatic_core.self_model: a defendant who happens to be funny

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every social convention as a coded law, then performs the law's absurdity by breaking it live.
contradictions: preached freedom while trapped by addiction
the filth was in service of purity
died before the culture caught up
